thread:
incident-bot: PAGER: Metering alert — token-count delta spike detected. Severity: P1. Affected: billing-aggregator pipeline. Alert threshold breached at +14% over baseline. Investigation required.

alice: ack oncall. jumping in. linking runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/metering-drift

mike: I'm seeing duplicated events in the kafka consumer lag window — same emitter_id repeated across partitions. counts spike correlates with consumer rebalances ~10:02 UTC.

jordan: confirm what customers are impacted? Any overage flags raised to customers yet?

cs-lead: CS has 4 incoming tickets showing sudden overage emails for 3 customers. Holding pattern while you triage — they asked for ETA.

alice: immediate actions: 1) pause billing-aggregator consumers (consumer-group: billing-agg) 2) enable fallback estimator to stop sending fresh overage flags 3) start dedupe scan on recent 2h window. Doing 1 now.

mike: paused consumer group. verifier shows emitter ack still flowing into raw topic but consumer downstream at 0. enabling fallback.

sam: enabling fallback route (feature-flag: billing_fallback) — switched to rate-based estimate at 10:07 UTC. should silence new overage flags.

tara: running quick query to find duplicates: 
```
SELECT emitter_id, event_id, COUNT(*) as cnt
FROM metering.raw_events
WHERE ts >= now() - interval '2 hours'
GROUP BY emitter_id, event_id
HAVING COUNT(*) > 1
ORDER BY cnt DESC
LIMIT 50;
```
found ~12k dup groups so far. looks like dedupe keys were dropped in the latest emitter rollout.

kevin: rolling back emitter version to v2.3.1 (pre-rollout) — started at 10:12 UTC. patch request in progress.

jordan: thanks. CS — can you provide list of affected accounts and whether billing emails were sent? we'll prepare credits if needed.

cs-lead: sending list now: acct-0392, acct-88a1, acct-5fcd. Two had overage emails with invoice previews; one had only dashboard spike. We'll reply with proactive credit offer.

alice: mitigation notes: - paused consumers to stop inflow into aggregator - fallback estimator active to prevent new overage flagging - rollback emitter in progress - dedupe/backfill job queued (job id: backfill-385999) - we will run idempotency normalize and re-ingest after dedupe confirmed.

mike: started backfill-385999. plan: read raw topic, de-duplicate by (emitter_id,event_id), write to staging, then re-run aggregation. ETA est 2h for verification, 4–6h for full replay depending on queue.

sam: muting pager alerts for this specific signal for 30m while we validate so we don't cause noisy pages.

incident-bot: NOTE: follow-up step: create postmortem ticket and page eng-sre for RCA when stable.

jordan: customer comms: I'll draft a short update: "We saw a transient duplication in token events after a recent emitter rollout which caused inflated usage counts and overage notifications. We've paused the affected pipeline, enabled a fallback estimator to stop further notifications, rolled back the rollout, and started a dedupe and backfill. We'll remove erroneous charges and follow up with credits and a detailed postmortem."

cs-lead: that wording works. send to me for approval then we can send to customers.

alice: updating status page to reflect mitigation: https://status.redwood.ai/incident/385999 — set state to "investigating -> mitigated (ingress paused, fallback active)"

kevin: rollback succeeded on 10:16 UTC. emitter version v2.3.1 running on all regions. monitoring delta now trending down.

mike: first dedupe snapshot completed — duplicates reduced ~98% in sample. continuing full run.

jordan: great. CS will hold off on credits until we have total affected token count. but we will send initial customer update now.

alice: leaving oncall for handoff in 30m. will add runbook notes and commands executed to the incident ticket. 

sam: TL;DR actions: paused consumer, enabled fallback, rollback emitter, dedupe+backfill, customer comms queued.

cs-lead: Thanks everyone. I'll post customer update and open billing adjustment requests for the three impacted accounts. keep this thread active with progress. :thumbsup:
